topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Etiology of cancer: Intrinsic luck, genetics, and environmental exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual framework of cancer causation by evaluating the relative contributions of endogenous mutations, inherited predispositions, and environmental risks supported by epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents drive malignancy, focusing in depth on the epidemiology and oncogenic mechanism of Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and dietary or chemical mutagens cause DNA damage, particularly through xenobiotic metabolic activation into reactive DNA adducts.

topics.label: Tumor promoters, inflammation, and host developmental susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish non-mutagenic tumor promotion and inflammatory signaling from initiation, highlighting how tissue microenvironments and host life stages enable malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and assessing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro techniques used to prove carcinogenicity, concluding with the practical evaluation of risk versus benefit.
